items.stem: In the given figure, PA and PB are tangents from external point P to a circle with centre C and Q is any point on the circle. Then the measure of ∠AQB is
items.answer: PA and PB touch the circle at A and B, so CA ⊥ PA and CB ⊥ PB. In quadrilateral PACB the two right angles leave ∠ACB + ∠APB = 180°, so ∠ACB = 180° − 55° = 125°. The angle ∠AQB at the circumference stands on the same arc AB as the central angle ∠ACB, so ∠AQB = ½ × ∠ACB = ½ × 125° = 62½°.
items.concept: Two equal tangents from an exterior point
items.ocr: Option (a) is printed as the mixed fraction 62½°; written here in Unicode. Figure cropped from the question (the book prints it above the options, not inside the solution).

items.stem: From an external point Q, the length of tangent to a circle is 12 cm and the distance of Q from the centre of circle is 13 cm. The radius of circle (in cm) is
items.answer: Let O be the centre and P the point of contact, so OQ = 13 cm and PQ = 12 cm. The radius is perpendicular to the tangent at the point of contact, hence OP ⊥ PQ and △OPQ is right angled at P. By Pythagoras, OP² + PQ² = OQ², so OP² = 13² − 12² = 169 − 144 = 25. Therefore the radius OP = 5 cm.

items.stem: QP is a tangent to a circle with centre O at a point P on the circle. If △OPQ is isosceles, then ∠OQR equals.
items.answer: The radius and the tangent are perpendicular at the point of contact, so ∠OPQ = 90°. In △OPQ the angles add to 180°: ∠POQ + ∠OPQ + ∠OQP = 180°. Since the triangle is isosceles and the right angle is at P, the two equal sides subtend the two equal angles ∠POQ and ∠OQP, giving 2∠OQP + 90° = 180°. Hence ∠OQP = 45°.
